subject: Resilience buffer / SLA amendment request (Cloudline)
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@cloudline.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14 09:12 PDT
Subject: Resilience buffer request for SLA (Cloudline)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profiles but we have an internal procurement constraint we need to solve before signing. Our compliance group wants a temporary carve that reduces the strict uptime floor for our batched inference workloads while we complete a migration and can’t guarantee steady prefix cache behavior for 30–60 days.

Specifically we're asking whether Redwood will accept a 90-day "resilience buffer" where the standard uptime percentage for our batched endpoints would move from 99.95% to 99.90% for that window, in exchange for a cap on monthly service credits (we'd like to cap at 2% of monthly invoice).

Attached is our annotated SLA draft (Cloudline_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf). Our procurement timeline is tight — we'd like confirmation this week if possible so we can move to legal redlines.

Thanks,
Evan Brooks
Sr. Procurement Manager
Cloudline Systems

Attachments: Cloudline_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@cloudline.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-14 11:04 PDT
Subject: Re: Resilience buffer request for SLA (Cloudline)

Evan — thanks for the clear ask and the annotated draft. I read your note and discussed internally with Product. A few immediate thoughts:

- We can acknowledge a temporary resilience buffer, but we prefer to frame it around a "latency corridor" rather than lowering the uptime percentage. That keeps availability guarantees intact while giving you protection for transient latency spikes during migration.

- Proposed pragmatic alternative (high level): allow a 90-day resilience period where the uptime floor remains 99.95% but Latency-99 (per-region, per-endpoint) is permitted to exceed normal thresholds up to a defined corridor (e.g., +250ms) without triggering credits unless latency breach is sustained and coincident with throughput loss.

- For credits, we can offer a capped monthly recompense calculation rather than a fixed percent: credits accrue only when both (a) >30-minute sustained latency breach at 99th percentile AND (b) platform-wide throughput drops by >10% for the same period. If triggered, credits will be calculated as a pro-rata of impacted minutes relative to the billing period and then subject to a monthly cap.

I'll loop Ben and Marissa on precise numbers (cap, corridor width, and whether the cap is 1%, 1.5% or 2%). Ben — can you propose the commercial tradeoffs here (caps vs. onboarding credit)? Marissa — can you flag any legal constraints on phrasing / measurement windows?

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with Evan tomorrow to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-amendment.docx (draft amendment template)

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@cloudline.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Cloudline Procurement <procurement@cloudline.com>
Date: 2026-06-14 13:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Resilience buffer request for SLA (Cloudline)

Tessa — appreciate the fast reply and the alternative framing. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- We prefer a simple, auditable trigger and cap. The proposed dual-condition makes sense technically, but our legal team prefers a straightforward monthly cap number we can point to in the contract.

- Cloudline can accept a latency-corridor approach, but we'd like the monthly cap to be no higher than 1.5% of the monthly invoice for the resilience period.

- Also important: the carve should be scoped to the specific batched endpoints used in our migration plan, not all hosted endpoints globally.

If you can send an updated amendment showing the corridor width and the 1.5% cap (or your counter) we'll take it to legal for a quick review.

Thanks,
Evan

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@cloudline.com>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15 09:18 PDT
Subject: Re: Resilience buffer request for SLA (Cloudline)

Evan — thanks for the preference for simplicity. We reviewed options and here's a counterproposal we think balances risk and procurement needs:

1) Term and scope
- Resilience buffer: 90 days from go-live
- Scope: specific batched inference endpoints listed in Appendix A of the amendment (regional scoping only)

2) Latency corridor & measurement
- Latency corridor: Latency-99 may exceed normal thresholds by up to +600ms for batched endpoints during the resilience period.
- Credits only trigger if the latency breach is sustained for 30 consecutive minutes AND concurrent region-level throughput for those endpoints drops >10% vs baseline.

3) Credit calculation & cap
- If triggered, credit = (impacted minutes / total minutes in billing period) * monthly invoice for impacted endpoints.
- Monthly cap = 1.0% of the monthly invoice for the affected endpoints.

4) Commercial sweetener
- If Cloudline signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment for the impacted capacity within 30 days, Redwood will apply a one-time onboarding credit of $15,000 against the first invoice.

5) Next steps
- I've attached a simple calculation workbook (credit-calculation.xlsx) with sample scenarios.
- If the commercial terms look acceptable, Marissa will prepare the amendment language and a DocuSign envelope for legal redlines.

Let me know if you'd like to discuss on a call — happy to join.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: credit-calculation.xlsx

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@cloudline.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: Cloudline Procurement <procurement@cloudline.com>
Date: 2026-06-15 16:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Resilience buffer request for SLA (Cloudline)

Ben / Tessa — thanks for the clear counter. Cloudline is prepared to accept the latency-corridor approach and the 30-minute sustained window. A couple of small asks before legal signs off:

- Please reduce the onboarding credit to $10,000 (our CFO prefers a lower one-time concession).
- Confirm that the 1.0% monthly cap applies only to the impacted endpoints, not our entire Redwood bill.

If you can update the amendment to reflect those two items (1) onboarding credit $10k, (2) explicit per-endpoint monthly cap language, we'll route to legal and aim to sign this week.

Evan
Sr. Procurement Manager
Cloudline Systems
